title: Unify project layout plans across Sway and macOS
description: Define one deterministic, platform-independent project layout plan in dock-core and compile it through Sway on Agora and the installed Dock Control Accessibility helper on macOS. Replace the current equal-width Mac strip and Sway-only tabbed intent with shared browser-primary and tool-stack semantics while preserving explicit project bindings and unrelated windows.
design: dock-core owns semantic roles and normalized layout geometry. dock-linux maps the plan to Sway containers/marks; dock-mac resolves bound windows and visible display frames, then sends bounded SetFrame/Focus operations to Dock Control. Alfalfa remains the source of resource identity. Executors verify their applied state and fail on ambiguous or stale window bindings.
acceptance_criteria: A shared tested planner produces deterministic browser-primary/tool-stack placements for one through sixteen windows and explicit usable display bounds. Dock Mac applies the plan only to project-bound windows through Dock Control and verifies returned frames. Sway consumes the same semantic plan rather than hardcoding a separate layout policy. CLI and GUI expose recall/layout without moving unrelated windows. Unit tests cover geometry, roles, overflow, negative origins, idempotence, and invalid bounds; live macOS proof uses the installed permission-bearing helper.
notes: First verified slice implemented locally: dock-core now owns deterministic browser-primary/secondary-stack geometry with negative-origin, ambiguity, overflow, and single-window tests. dock-mac maps bound app identities to semantic browser/tool roles, applies only bound windows through Dock Control SetFrame, and raises the primary browser after placement. GUI uses the shared planner. Added cross-platform boundary documentation. Validation: dock-core 15 tests pass; dock-mac lib 42 pass/2 ignored; strict clippy for dock-core and dock-mac all targets passes. Full workspace rebuild was bounded by disk capacity after 957 MiB of a fresh target; generated targets were cleaned and 996 MiB restored. Remaining: Sway compiler consumes the same plan and live installed-helper macOS proof.

title: Keep local commit authority in Beads hooks without a remote
description: Beads 1.1.0 codex-hook injects Git authority: no git operations whenever a repository lacks a Git remote, even when no-git-ops=false, BD_AGENT_PROFILE=team-maintainer, and the FPL repository policy explicitly authorizes local commits. This prevents the local commits that preserve work even though commits do not require a remote.
design: Prefer an upstream-supported Beads fix or profile that separates commit authority from push/sync authority. Preserve bd remember injection and avoid custom PRIME.md because current Beads custom-prime behavior can drop persistent memories. Cover repositories with and without Git/Dolt remotes.
acceptance_criteria: Codex hook output permits local commits after validation under the FPL standing policy when no remote exists; it continues to forbid push and Dolt sync without a configured remote or separate authority; explicit do-not-commit still wins; persistent memories remain injected; tests cover remote and no-remote repositories.

acceptance_criteria: The canonical tenet states the standing commit authorization and separates it from remote operations; tests verify generated managed blocks; fpl sync propagates it without altering text outside managed markers; repository tests and doctor checks pass.
notes: Updated engineering-tenets canonical tenet 5 to authorize completed verified local commits by default while keeping push/merge/release/deploy/remote sync/history rewrites separately authorized. Added regression test and README guidance. cargo fmt check, 13 tests, strict Clippy, build and fpl doctor pass. fpl sync updated all discovered repositories and four global agent contexts; second pass reported 156/156 targets current. Engineering-tenets local Beads database was malformed and remote bootstrap reported a phantom/non-clonable Dolt ref, so tracking remained in Dock. title: Decide managed Firefox terms handling for isolated project profiles

design: Choose between explicit one-time owner acceptance per profile, an owner-authorized managed SkipTermsOfUse policy, or a browser profile/container design that preserves isolation without repeated onboarding. Mozilla documents that enabling SkipTermsOfUse represents acceptance and authority on behalf of every user, so Dock must not enable it implicitly.
acceptance_criteria: The owner makes the policy decision explicitly; project recall either opens ready content or returns a deterministic actionable state; no acceptance preferences are forged or copied; tests cover fresh and accepted profiles; the manual runbook documents recovery.

No credential or private context content appears in tool results. Unknown identities and malformed or ambiguous metadata fail visibly. With one browser and one terminal, browser receives the primary area. With multiple browsers/tools, browsers remain usable rather than narrow vertical slices and secondary panes stack predictably. Unit tests cover plan derivation and tree validation; live Dock and Studio proof preserves sessions across recall.

design: Keep the MCP server and extension colocated with the browser they control. Do not forward Browser MCP's WebSocket port through Dock or expose it on LAN/Tailscale. OpenCode/Edgerunner remains the MCP client owner; Dock supplies project identity and existing human-takeover authorization. Pin a reviewed version and extension identity for any spike. Compare against the current dock-linux browser API and call the existing owner instead of duplicating automation logic.
acceptance_criteria: Document the published server and extension versions tested; verify actual listen address and whether the extension/server channel authenticates; reject any default 0.0.0.0 or unauthenticated control path unless isolated by a maintained upstream configuration; prove a browser action only in an explicitly attached project profile on Mac and Agora; verify another project/profile cannot be read or controlled; verify human takeover revokes agent browser operations; measure idle and repeated-action memory; preserve browser login across restart without exporting cookies; compare reliability and tool surface with Dock's current browser operations; record an adopt, wrap, or reject decision and remove all spike services/extensions if rejected.

title: Prototype custom compositing client after exhausting stock remoting
description: Mesh §§3,8 long-term. Evaluate moonlight-common-c decode and ScreenCaptureKit capture for local/remote texture compositing. Preserve transport/core boundary and only use opaque video when structural access is unavailable. Acceptance: benchmark against working stock Sunshine/Moonlight before replacement.

title: Replace Sway backend with Smithay after core daily-use validation
description: Mesh §§2,7,8. Future phase only after Mac AX and pane interfaces prove stable. Implement the same backend contract using Smithay without changing upstream profile or orchestration semantics. Acceptance: backend contract and daily-use parity tests.

title: Build session gateway with structural pane access and existing identity
description: Mesh §§3–5,8. Expose background agents as PTY/structural panes, reuse Tailscale and FPL OIDC, support PTY convergence and CDP/AX structural access. Keep opaque streaming on demand and Shroud GPU-free. Acceptance: authenticated local/remote panes share addressing and reconnect semantics.
notes: User identifies Edge Runner as long-term owner/host for OpenCode sessions, with Codex/Claude sessions potentially on Agora One. Investigate actual existing session interfaces before designing adapters. Desired capability: agent and human can locate, manage and prompt sessions through project workspace orchestration, with explicit takeover and lifecycle behavior.

title: Resolve session locality, persistence, dispatch and shared-node identity
description: Mesh §9. Decide per-VM versus pooled session gateway, Shroud suspend/resume versus reopen-on-boot, dispatch_task relationship, and multi-person node arbitration. Record decisions in Beads before implementing affected contracts.

title: Formalize profile contract and connect JARVIS tier-1 activation
description: Mesh §§2,5,8. Migrate proven v0 profile format to the real core, keeping executors replaceable. Call the existing JARVIS deterministic tier-1 action owner; do not rebuild agency. Acceptance: voice and UI activate identical profiles through the same interface.

title: Implement pane-tree layout core and public macOS AX backend
description: Mesh §§2,7,8 phase Next. Define PTY/CDP/AX/opaque handles and pure layout-to-rectangles interface; implement toggleable AX move/resize/focus/observe without SIP-gated APIs. Acceptance: deterministic layout tests and daily-driver Mac validation, with no transport or compute internals in the core.
notes: User explicitly wants local Mac tiling and quick switching between related Linux and Mac windows by project. Preserve direct human control. Evaluate AX/public APIs and existing capabilities; do not assume whole-desktop streaming provides individual remote-window control.

title: Computing mesh after Dock v0: orchestration and session roadmap
description: Architectural reference and conditional future candidates from computing-mesh design, not an approved build queue. First learn from a usable Linux desktop streamed to Mac. Existing JARVIS, Shroud, Tailscale, OIDC and Coherence remain owned externally; only demonstrated integration gaps belong here. Reassess pane core, profile formalization, session gateway, compositor and custom client against current implementations before scheduling.

title: Resolve long-term profile and Coherence artifact ownership
description: First-cut §7. Initial boundary: vendored upstream token JSON produces shared runtime JSON plus Waybar CSS. Decide refresh ownership and profile location with Coherence; reserve JARVIS integration contract without implementing agency.
